tagline: A real ledger. Fake money. <brand>Zero shortcuts.</brand>
cta: I built a personal banking app end to end — accounts, deposits, and instant transfers, backed by a real Go ledger service.
featureAccountsDesc: Create, edit, and delete accounts — deleting one automatically sweeps its balance to another, so money never just vanishes.
featureTransfersDesc: Pick a recent destination and move money between accounts in one atomic call. No partial transfers.
featureSecurityDesc: Every request carries a session cookie through one shared interceptor. A single 401, anywhere, logs you out everywhere.
unsavedChangesDescription: You have unsaved changes. If you leave now, they will be lost.

nav.productDescription: Everything you need to manage your money in one place.

hero.eyebrow: A full-stack side project, not a SaaS pitch
hero.ctaHint: Yes, it's fake money — the ledger math doesn't know that.

problem.title: Money spread across accounts is hard to keep straight.
problem.description: I wanted to build something harder than a to-do app. Juggling currencies, balances, and transfers is a surprisingly easy way to get state consistency wrong.

points.title: Scattered balances
points.description: Multiple accounts and currencies is really a multi-row consistency problem wearing a banking UI.

points.title: Slow transfers
points.description: A transfer touches two account rows at once — get the transaction boundary wrong and money duplicates or disappears.

points.title: Security worries
points.description: Session handling isn't decorative. Get it wrong and it's not a UX bug, it's a data breach.

solution.title: One place for every account — and a ledger keeping it honest.
solution.description: Create as many accounts as you want, deposit into any of them, and transfer between them instantly. Delete an account and its balance sweeps automatically to another — in a ledger, money doesn't just disappear.

features.title: Three features. Here's the actual mechanism behind each one.

architecture.title: One request, five hops, zero magic.
architecture.subtitle: I could tell you it's "built with modern best practices." Or I could just show you exactly what happens when you click a button.

steps.title: Client Component
steps.description: A form or button. It calls a feature hook — it never touches Axios directly.

steps.title: hooks/query.ts
steps.description: TanStack Query — useQuery/useMutation, plus a queryKeys factory shared with the server.

steps.title: client.ts
steps.description: A typed resource client — one class per domain, one method per endpoint.

steps.title: apiClient + interceptor
steps.description: One Axios instance, one interceptor, attached exactly once — auth header, timezone header, request logging.

steps.title: Go core-service
steps.description: The real ledger lives here. This app doesn't touch a database — it just asks nicely over HTTP.

prefetch.label: + SSR prefetch on first load
prefetch.description: Every page also prefetches with this exact same query key on the server, then hands the cache to the browser. First paint already has real data — zero loading flash.

callouts: Every API call is typed end to end — from the Zod-validated form, to the Axios client, to the response envelope the Go service returns. If the backend changes its shape, TypeScript tells me before a user does.
One Axios instance, one interceptor, attached exactly once — there's a WeakSet guard for that. Every request gets an auth header without a single feature file importing Axios directly.
